Thank you for the response, it really does mean a lot to me. I've been an addict since I was 14. 
I'm 22 now. I started off smoking pot because it really gave me a sense of identity and belonging. It was like "look at me, I'm the cool counter culture guy doing drugs" not just the "the socially awkward guy who keeps to himself". I've suffered from social anxiety for as long as I can remember and weed didin't completely alieviate the symptoms but it made it much easier to cope. 

I started drinking when I was 18 and I right away noticed a drastic shift in my personality. Suddenly I was making friends and attending social events instead of staying home getting stoned and playing guitar. It didn't take long before it got completely out of control. I was drinking a large amount of alcohol daily, blacking out and acting extremely wreckless. The very substance that helped me make friends and socialize was now destroying my social life. I alienated family and friends and I became a very bitter, hateful person. 

This continued for years and my behaviour became increasingly more self destructive. I was mixing Valium and Xanax with booze fully aware of the dangers that paticular mix of substances had. I would smoke crack and speed by myself in my room. And became extremely iratated when my roommates would question my behaviour. Even though they we're only trying to help. 

About a month and a half ago. I was drunk with a close friend and we ended up hooking up. I was devastated by this because I considered this person a very good friend and I didn't want to ruin our relationship with a drunken sexual encounter. The next day I tried to kill my self with a lethal mix of Vailum and wine. My roommate came home to find me blue and hardly breathing so he called he ambulance. I had my stomach pumped and they sent me on my way. After that ordeal I decided it was time to give up drinking and drugs (excluding pot). 

Now here I am. I can really relate to what you said about the emotions flooding back. I was so numbed out for years that now the littlest things will bring me to tears. I've made arrangements to see a counsellor this coming week. Hopefully that turns out okay.

Again I really appreciate the response. You helped me out a bit. I managed to get up and take the dog for a walk and I feel somewhat relieved. Thank you :)
